question.text: Cat III AIFs typically implement short positions in Indian equities through which mechanism?

answer.text: Stock Lending and Borrowing (SLB) via exchange OR derivatives (futures/options on stock).
Short-selling is prohibited for Cat III AIFs.

explanation.text: The Logic: Indian markets do not permit naked short-selling by institutional investors. Cat III AIFs short via SLB segment (cash-market short with borrowed securities) OR via equity derivatives (short futures / buy puts / sell calls). The Trap: A is banned (naked short). C is fabricated settlement cycle. D is wrong — shorts are permitted. Cross-Exam Context: VIII covers SLB/derivatives. XIX-C same. XXI-B PMS generally cannot short.
